issues.issue: What standard of review applies to the RPD's interpretation of Article 1F(b)?
issues.applicant_position: Correctness applies; the presumption of reasonableness is rebutted for an international convention provision.
issues.respondent_position: Takes no position; argues the appeal fails under either standard of review.
issues.result_quote: Correctness review is more likely than reasonableness review to achieve this goal, and is therefore the standard to be applied

issues.issue: Is rehabilitation or present dangerousness relevant to whether a non-political crime is serious under Article 1F(b)?
issues.applicant_position: Seriousness must consider rehabilitation and present danger; the RPD erred by ignoring them.
issues.respondent_position: Intervener (MPSEP) argued exclusion follows from the convictions; rehabilitation and present danger are irrelevant.
issues.result_quote: Article 1F (b) should be interpreted as excluding rehabilitation and present dangerousness from the assessment of the seriousness of a crime

issues.issue: Does the statutory context of IRPA (ineligibility, PRRA, rehabilitation provisions) support a narrower reading of Article 1F(b)?
issues.applicant_position: The IRPA scheme makes rehabilitation relevant, so a broad reading of Article 1F(b) is inconsistent with it.
issues.result_quote: there is, in my view, no inconsistency between a broad interpretation of Article 1F (b) and other provisions of the IRPA dealing with criminality
